title.zh: 卷一百〇三 列傳第五十三: 郭虔瓘 張嵩 郭知運 王君 張守珪 牛仙客 王忠嗣
title.en: Volume 103 Biographies 53: Guo Qianguan, Zhang Song, Guo Zhiyun, Wang Jun, Zhang Shougui, Niu Xianke, Wang Zhongsi
title.raw: 卷一百〇三 列傳第五十三: 郭虔瓘 張嵩 郭知運 王君 張守珪 牛仙客 王忠嗣 Volume 103 Biographies 53: Guo Qianguan, Zhang Song, Guo Zhiyun, Wang Jun, Zhang Shougui, Niu Xianke, Wang Zhongsi

sentences.zh: 郭虔瓘，齊州歷城人也。

translations.literal: Guo Qianguan was a man of Licheng in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qianguan was a native of Licheng in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 開元初，累遷右驍衛將軍，兼北庭都護。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, he was repeatedly promoted to General of the Right Xiaowei Guards and concurrently Protector-General of Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign, he rose through successive appointments to general of the Right Xiaowei Guards and concurrent protector-general of Beiting.

sentences.zh: 二年春，突厥默啜遣其子移江可汗及同俄特勒率精騎圍逼北庭，虔瓘率眾固守。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year, the Turkic qaghan Mochuo sent his son the Yijiang Khan and the tegin Tong'e leading elite cavalry to surround and press Beiting; Qianguan led the masses in stout defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Kaiyuan 2, the Turkic qaghan Mochuo sent his son the Yijiang Khan and the tegin Tong'e at the head of elite horsemen to besiege Beiting, and Qianguan held the city with his troops.

sentences.zh: 同俄特勒單騎親逼城下，虔瓘使勇士伏於路左，突起斬之。

translations.literal: Tong'e tegin came alone on horseback to press close beneath the walls in person; Qianguan had brave men lie in ambush to the left of the road and abruptly rose up and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Tong'e tegin rode up alone to the foot of the walls; Qianguan had warriors lie in wait along the road to the left and sprang out to cut him down.

sentences.zh: 賊眾既至，失同俄，相率於城下乞降，請盡軍中衣資器杖以贖同俄。

translations.literal: When the rebel host arrived and lost Tong'e, they followed one another in begging surrender below the walls, asking to give up all clothing, supplies, and weapons in the army to ransom Tong'e.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy force arrived and found Tong'e gone, they gathered beneath the walls to beg surrender, offering to hand over all clothing, gear, and arms in the camp to ransom him.

sentences.zh: 及聞其死，三軍慟哭，便引退。

translations.literal: When they heard of his death, the entire army wailed in grief and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Once they learned he was dead, the whole army broke into mourning wails and then pulled back.

sentences.zh: 默啜女婿火拔頡利發石阿失畢時與同俄特勒同領兵，以同俄之死，懼不敢歸，遂將其妻歸降。

translations.literal: Mochuo's son-in-law Huoba yabghu and Shia A-shi-pi were at that time leading troops together with Tong'e tegin; because of Tong'e's death they feared and dared not return, and so brought their wives and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo's son-in-law Huoba yabghu and Shia A-shi-pi were then campaigning with Tong'e tegin; terrified by Tong'e's death, they dared not go home and came over with their wives in surrender.

sentences.zh: 虔瓘以破賊之功，拜冠軍大將軍，行右驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: For his achievement in defeating the enemy, Qianguan was appointed Champion General-in-Chief and Acting General-in-Chief of the Right Xiaowei Guards.
translations.idiomatic: For breaking the enemy, Qianguan was made champion general-in-chief and acting general-in-chief of the Right Xiaowei Guards.

sentences.zh: 又下制曰：

translations.literal: Another edict was also issued, stating:
translations.idiomatic: An edict was also promulgated, which read:

sentences.zh: 朕聞賞有功、報有德者，政之急也。

translations.literal: We have heard that rewarding those with achievement and requiting those with virtue are the urgent matters of government.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that rewarding merit and repaying virtue are the foremost duties of rule.

sentences.zh: 若功不賞，德不報，則人何謂哉。

translations.literal: If achievement is not rewarded and virtue not requited, what are people to say?
translations.idiomatic: If deeds go unrewarded and kindness unreturned, what will men make of it?

sentences.zh: 雲麾將軍、檢校右驍衛將軍，兼北庭都護、翰海軍經略使、金山道副大總管、招慰營田等使、上柱國、太原縣開國子郭虔瓘，宣威將軍、守右驍衛翊府中郎將、檢校伊州刺史兼伊吾軍使、借紫金魚袋、上柱國郭知運等，早負名節，見稱義勇。

translations.literal: Yunhui General, Acting General of the Right Xiaowei Guards, concurrently Protector-General of Beiting, Commissioner for the Hanhai Army, Vice Grand Commander of the Jinshan Circuit, Commissioner for Reassurance and Frontier Agriculture, Shangzhuguo, and Viscount of Taixuan Guo Qianguan; Xuanwei General, Defender of the Right Xiaowei Yifu Central Commandant, Acting Governor of Yizhou and Commissioner of the Yiwu Army, on loan the gold-purple fish tally, Shangzhuguo Guo Zhiyun, and others—long bore reputation and integrity and were acclaimed for righteousness and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qianguan—yunhui general, acting general of the Right Xiaowei Guards, concurrent protector-general of Beiting, Hanhai army commissioner, vice grand commander of the Jinshan circuit, commissioner for reassurance and frontier agriculture, shangzhuguo, and founding viscount of Taixuan—and Guo Zhiyun—xuanwei general, defender of the Right Xiaowei yifu central commandant, acting governor of Yizhou and commissioner of the Yiwu army, lent the gold-purple fish tally, shangzhuguo—and the rest have long been known for honor and are praised as men of righteous valor.

sentences.zh: 頃者柳中、金滿，偏師禦敵，蕭條窮漠之外，奔迫孤城之下。

translations.literal: Recently at Liuzhong and Jinman, a detached force resisted the enemy, in desolate lands beyond the farthest desert, pressed in flight beneath lonely walls.
translations.idiomatic: Only lately, at Liuzhong and Jinman, a flank force held off the foe in bleak country beyond the farthest wastes, harried beneath beleaguered walls.

sentences.zh: 強寇益侵，援兵不至，既守而戰，自秋涉冬，櫪馬長嘶，戍人遠望。

translations.literal: Strong enemies pressed ever closer, reinforcements did not arrive; they defended and fought, from autumn through winter; stable horses whinnied long, garrison men gazed from afar.
translations.idiomatic: As stronger foes pressed in and relief never came, they fought behind the walls from autumn into winter; horses in the stalls neighed without cease while the garrison watched the horizon.

sentences.zh: 謀以十勝，成其九拒。

translations.literal: They plotted with ten points for victory and achieved nine for refusal.
translations.idiomatic: They laid plans for ten victories and brought nine of them to bear in holding the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 遂能摧日逐之遺種，斬天驕之愛息。

translations.literal: Thus they were able to crush the remnant seed of the Rìzhú and behead the beloved heir of Heaven's pride.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they shattered the remnant line of the Xiongnu and struck down the cherished son of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 豈耿恭、班超，獨高前史；

translations.literal: Were Geng Gong and Ban Chao alone exalted in former histories?
translations.idiomatic: Are Geng Gong and Ban Chao alone to tower over the annals of old?

sentences.zh: 將廉頗、李牧，與朕同時。

translations.literal: The likes of Lian Po and Li Mu share our time with Us.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Lian Po and Li Mu walk the earth in Our own age.

sentences.zh: 眷言茂勛，是所嘉嘆。

translations.literal: Regarding their lush achievements, this is what We laud and sigh over.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on their splendid merit, We can only praise and marvel.

sentences.zh: 信可以疇其井邑，昭示遐邇，俾勞臣觀而懦夫立焉。

translations.literal: Truly they can be granted fiefs within their settlements and made manifest to far and near, making laboring ministers gaze upon them and timid men stand firm.
translations.idiomatic: Surely they deserve estates of their own, held up as examples to the distant and the near, so that weary servants of the state may take heart and cowards find their footing.

sentences.zh: 虔瓘可進封太原郡開國公，知運可封介休縣開國公。

translations.literal: Qianguan may be advanced to enfeoffment as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery; Zhiyun may be enfeoffed as Duke of Jiexiu County.
translations.idiomatic: Qianguan shall be advanced to founding duke of Taiyuan commandery; Zhiyun shall be made founding duke of Jiexiu county.

sentences.zh: 虔瓘俄轉安西副大都護、攝御史大夫、四鎮經略安撫使，進封潞國公，賜實封一百戶虔瓘及奏請募關中兵一萬人往安西討擊，皆給公乘，兼供熟食，敕許之。

translations.literal: Qianguan soon transferred to Vice Protector-General of Anxi, Acting Censor-in-Chief, Commissioner for Pacification of the Four Garrisons, advanced to Duke of Lu, granted a substantive fief of one hundred households; Qianguan also memorialized requesting to recruit ten thousand soldiers from Guanzhong to go to Anxi for punitive attacks, all to be given government carts and also supplied cooked food—an edict permitted this.
translations.idiomatic: Qianguan was soon made vice protector-general of Anxi, acting censor-in-chief, and commissioner for pacification of the Four Garrisons, advanced to duke of Lu with a substantive fief of one hundred households. He also asked to raise ten thousand Guanzhong troops for a punitive campaign in Anxi, with government transport and cooked rations for all; the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠韋湊上疏曰：

translations.literal: Director of Palace Works Wei Cou submitted a memorial, stating:
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cou, director of palace works, submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞兵者兇器，不護己而用之。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that arms are inauspicious implements and are not used without regard for oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that war is an ill-omened tool, not to be wielded without weighing one's own safety.

sentences.zh: 今西域諸蕃，莫不順軌。

translations.literal: Now all the various tribes of the Western Regions none fail to follow the track.
translations.idiomatic: At present every tribe of the Western Regions follows the imperial track without exception.

sentences.zh: 縱鼠竊狗盜，有戍卒鎮兵，足宣式遏之威，非降赫斯之怒。

translations.literal: Even if rats steal and dogs pilfer, there are garrison soldiers and stationed troops, sufficient to proclaim the authority of restraint and deterrence, not to lower Heaven's wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Even petty raids by bandits can be met by frontier garrisons, enough to display restraining might without summoning Heaven's full wrath upon the realm.

sentences.zh: 此師之出，未見其名。

translations.literal: This army's going forth—its name is not yet seen.
translations.idiomatic: As for this expedition, no clear enemy justifies it.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞安不忘危，理必資備。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that in security one does not forget danger; principle necessarily relies on preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has also heard that in peace one must not forget peril, and that good order depends on readiness.

sentences.zh: 自近及遠，強幹弱枝，是以漢實關中，徙諸豪族。

translations.literal: From near to far, strengthen the trunk and weaken the branches; thus the Han filled Guanzhong and moved all the powerful clans.
translations.idiomatic: Policy should strengthen the center before the periphery; that is why the Han peopled Guanzhong and relocated the great clans there.

sentences.zh: 今關輔戶口，積久逋逃，承前先虛，見猶未實。

translations.literal: Now the household registers of Guanfu have long accumulated absconders; inheriting prior emptiness, what is seen is still not solid.
translations.idiomatic: Household registers in the Guanzhong region have long been hollowed by flight and evasion; figures inherited from earlier years remain unreliable even now.

sentences.zh: 屬北虜犯塞，西戎駭邊，凡在丁壯，征行略盡。

translations.literal: Just as northern barbarians violated the passes and western Rong alarmed the borders, all who were adult males in military service were largely exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: With northern foes raiding the frontier and western tribes striking the borders, able-bodied men have already been nearly drained by campaigns.

sentences.zh: 豈宜更募驍勇，遠資荒服。

translations.literal: How is it fitting to recruit more fierce warriors to supply distant wild domains?
translations.idiomatic: How can it be right to raise more elite troops to feed some distant wilderness?

sentences.zh: 又一萬行人，詣六千餘里，咸給遞馱，並供熟食，道次州縣，將何以供？

translations.literal: Moreover ten thousand men on the march, going more than six thousand li, all given relay pack animals and also supplied cooked food—how will the prefectures and counties along the route supply them?
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand men marching more than six thousand li, each with relay mounts and hot meals—what prefecture or county along the way can bear that burden?

sentences.zh: 秦、隴之西，人戶漸少，涼州已去，沙磧悠然。

translations.literal: West of Qin and Long, households gradually grow fewer; once Liangzhou is passed, the sandy wastes stretch on endlessly.
translations.idiomatic: West of Qin and Long the population thins; beyond Liangzhou lies nothing but endless desert.

sentences.zh: 遣彼居人，如何得濟？

translations.literal: Sending those inhabitants there, how can they be saved?
translations.idiomatic: How are the people along that route to survive it?

sentences.zh: 又萬人賞賜，費用極多；

translations.literal: Moreover rewards for ten thousand men entail extremely great expense;
translations.idiomatic: Rewards for ten thousand men alone would cost a fortune;

sentences.zh: 萬里資糧，破損尤廣。

translations.literal: provisions for ten thousand li—the damage and loss are especially vast.
translations.idiomatic: and supplies for a march of ten thousand li would waste the treasury on an even greater scale.

sentences.zh: 縱令必克，其獲幾何？

translations.literal: Even supposing certain victory, how much would be gained?
translations.idiomatic: Even if victory were certain, what would the gain amount to?

sentences.zh: 儻稽天誅，無乃甚損！

translations.literal: If Heaven's punishment is delayed, would not the loss be very great!
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven withholds success, the harm would be ruinous indeed!

sentences.zh: 請令計議所用所得，校其多少，即知利害。

translations.literal: I request that the expenditure and gains be calculated and compared in amount; then profit and harm will be known.
translations.idiomatic: Let the costs and expected gains be reckoned side by side; the balance of profit and loss will speak for itself.

sentences.zh: 況用者必賞，獲者未量，何要此行，頓空畿甸。

translations.literal: Moreover those who are used must be rewarded, while what is obtained is not yet measured—why require this expedition and suddenly empty the capital region?
translations.idiomatic: Those sent must be rewarded whether or not victory comes, while the spoils remain uncertain—why drain the capital districts for such a march?

sentences.zh: 且上古之時，大同之化，不獨子子，不獨親親，何隔華戎，務均安靖。

translations.literal: Moreover in high antiquity, under the transformation of Great Unity, one did not treat only one's own sons as sons nor only one's own kin as kin—why separate Chinese and Rong, striving equally for peace and stability?
translations.idiomatic: In high antiquity, under the reign of Great Unity, men did not cherish only their own children or kin—why should Chinese and barbarian be divided when the aim is universal peace?

sentences.zh: 洎皇道謝古，帝德慚皇，猶尚綏懷，不從征伐，有占風覘雨之客，無越海逾山之師。

translations.literal: Down to when the imperial Way declined from antiquity and imperial virtue fell short of the August Ones, they still prized soothing and cherishing, not following punitive campaigns—there were guests who observed wind and watched rain, but no armies crossing seas and surpassing mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the sage way faded and later emperors fell short of the ancients, rulers still favored reassurance over conquest; they kept observers of wind and rain, not armies that crossed seas and mountains.

sentences.zh: 其後漢武膺圖，誌恢土宇，西通絕域，北擊匈奴。

translations.literal: Afterward Emperor Wu of Han received the mandate, his ambition to restore territory; west he connected with utmost domains, north he struck the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Wu of Han took the throne resolved to recover the realm, opening the far west and striking the Xiongnu in the north.

sentences.zh: 雖廣獲珍奇，多斬首級，而中國疲耗，殆至危亡。

translations.literal: Although he broadly obtained rare treasures and beheaded many, yet the Central States were exhausted and depleted, nearly reaching peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Though he won rare treasures and heaps of enemy heads, the heartland was worn to exhaustion and nearly brought to ruin.

sentences.zh: 是以俗號昇平君稱盛德者，鹹指唐堯之代，不歸漢武之年。

translations.literal: Thus those commonly called the Age of Ascending Peace or praised for flourishing virtue all point to the era of Tang Yao, not to the years of Han Wu.
translations.idiomatic: That is why ages praised as peaceful and virtuous are always traced to the time of Yao, never to the reign of Han Wudi.

sentences.zh: 其要功不成者，復焉足比議？

translations.literal: As for one whose essential achievement is not accomplished, how is he worth comparing in discussion?
translations.idiomatic: If success is unlikely from the outset, what comparison with those examples is even worth making?

sentences.zh: 惟陛下圖之。

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty should consider it.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 虔瓘竟無克獲之功。

translations.literal: Qianguan in the end had no achievement of conquest and capture.
translations.idiomatic: Qianguan ultimately won no decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 尋遷右威衛大將軍，以疾卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Weiwu Guards and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made general-in-chief of the Right Weiwu Guards and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 其後，又以張嵩為安西都護以代虔瓘。

translations.literal: Afterward, Zhang Song was again made Protector-General of Anxi to replace Qianguan.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Song was appointed protector-general of Anxi in Qianguan's place.

sentences.zh: 嵩身長七尺，偉姿儀。

translations.literal: Song was seven chi in height, with imposing bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Song stood seven chi tall, with a commanding presence.

sentences.zh: 初進士舉，常以邊任自許。

translations.literal: When he first passed the jinshi examination, he often pledged himself to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he passed the jinshi examination, he styled himself a man for the frontier.

sentences.zh: 及在安西，務農重戰，安西府庫，遂為充實。

translations.literal: When he was in Anxi, he devoted effort to agriculture and valued warfare; the Anxi treasury thus became full and solid.
translations.idiomatic: In Anxi he stressed farming and readiness for war, and the Anxi treasury grew ample.

sentences.zh: 十年，轉太原尹，卒官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Prefect of Taiyuan and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became prefect of Taiyuan and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 俄又以黃門侍郎杜暹代嵩為安西都護。

translations.literal: Soon Yellow Gate Attendant-Censor Du Xian was again made Protector-General of Anxi to replace Song.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Du Xian, attendant-censor of the Yellow Gate, replaced Song as protector-general of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 郭知運字逢時，瓜州常樂人。

translations.literal: Guo Zhiyun, style Fengshi, was a man of Changle in Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhiyun, courtesy name Fengshi, was a native of Changle in Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 壯勇善射，頗有膽略。

translations.literal: Stalwart and brave, skilled in archery, he possessed considerable daring and resource.
translations.idiomatic: Strong and fearless, an expert archer, he was notably bold and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 初為秦州三度府果毅，以戰功累除左驍衛中郎將、瀚海軍經略使，又轉檢校伊州刺史，兼伊吾軍使。

translations.literal: He first served as guoyi of the Sandu Office in Qinzhou; through military achievements he was repeatedly promoted to Central Commandant of the Left Xiaowei Guards, Commissioner for the Hanhai Army, then transferred to Acting Governor of Yizhou and concurrently Commissioner of the Yiwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a guoyi officer in Qinzhou's Sandu office and, on the strength of battle honors, rose to central commandant of the Left Xiaowei Guards and Hanhai army commissioner, then became acting governor of Yizhou and commissioner of the Yiwu army.

sentences.zh: 開元二年春，副郭虔瓘破突厥於北庭，以功封介休縣公，加雲麾將軍，擢拜右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: In spring of Kaiyuan 2, as deputy to Guo Qianguan he defeated the Turks at Beiting; for his achievement he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jiexiu County, added Yunhui General, and promoted to General of the Right Wuwei Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Kaiyuan 2 he served under Guo Qianguan in defeating the Turks at Beiting and, for his merit, was made duke of Jiexiu county, given the rank of yunhui general, and promoted to general of the Right Wuwei Guards.

sentences.zh: 其秋，吐蕃入寇隴右，掠監牧馬而去，詔知運率眾擊之。

translations.literal: That autumn the Tibetans invaded Longyou, plundered the imperial pasture horses, and departed; an edict ordered Zhiyun to lead troops to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Tibetans raided Longyou, drove off the imperial stud horses, and withdrew; Zhiyun was ordered to take troops after them.

sentences.zh: 知運與薛訥、王皎等掎角擊敗之，拜知運鄯州都督、隴右諸軍節度大使。

translations.literal: Zhiyun with Xue Ne, Wang Jiao, and others attacked from converging angles and defeated them; Zhiyun was appointed Military Governor of Binzhou and Grand Commissioner of the Longyou Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyun, Xue Ne, Wang Jiao, and others caught the enemy in a pincer and routed them; Zhiyun was made military governor of Binzhou and grand commissioner of the Longyou armies.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，突厥降戶阿悉爛、⻊夾跌思太等率眾反叛，單於副都護張知運為賊所執，詔薛訥領兵討之。

translations.literal: In winter of the fourth year, surrendered Turk households led by A-xi-lan, Jia-die-si-tai, and others rose in rebellion; Vice Protector-General of Chanyu Zhang Zhiyun was seized by the rebels; an edict ordered Xue Ne to lead troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Kaiyuan 4, surrendered Turks led by A-xi-lan and Jia-die-si-tai rebelled; Zhang Zhiyun, vice protector-general of Chanyu, was captured, and Xue Ne was sent to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 叛賊至綏州界，詔知運領朔方兵募橫擊之，大破賊眾於黑山呼延谷，賊舍甲仗並棄張知運走。

translations.literal: When the rebels reached the border of Suizhou, an edict ordered Zhiyun to lead Shuofang troops and levies to strike them across their path; he greatly defeated the rebel host at Hushan Huyan Valley; the rebels abandoned armor and weapons and also abandoned Zhang Zhiyun and fled.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels reached Suizhou, Guo Zhiyun was ordered to lead Shuofang troops in a flank attack and crushed them at Hushan Huyan Valley; the enemy threw down arms and fled, leaving Zhang Zhiyun behind.

sentences.zh: 六年，知運又率兵入討吐蕃，賊徒無備，遂掩至九曲，獲鎖及甲馬耗牛等數萬計。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Zhiyun again led troops in to attack the Tibetans; the rebels were unprepared, and he suddenly reached Jiuqu, capturing shackles, armor, horses, yak cattle, and the like numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhiyun again marched against Tibet; catching the enemy unawares, he swept to Jiuqu and seized tens of thousands of shackles, arms, horses, and yaks.

sentences.zh: 知運獻捷，遂分賜京文武五品已上清官及朝集使，拜知運為兼鴻臚卿、攝御史中丞，加封太原郡公。

translations.literal: Zhiyun presented the victory report; spoils were then distributed to civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above in the capital, qingguan, and assembly envoys; Zhiyun was appointed Concurrent Minister of Ceremonies, Acting Vice Censor-in-Chief, and advanced to Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhiyun reported his victory, the spoils were shared among capital officials of the fifth rank and above and the assembly envoys; he was made concurrent minister of ceremonies and acting vice censor-in-chief and advanced to duke of Taiyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 八年，六州胡康待賓等反，詔知運與王皎討平之，拜左武衛大將軍，授一子官，賜金銀器百事、雜彩千段。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Six Prefectures Hu led by Kang Dai-bin and others rebelled; an edict ordered Zhiyun and Wang Jiao to suppress and pacify them; he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Wuwei Guards, one son was granted an office, and he was given one hundred items of gold and silver vessels and a thousand lengths of variegated silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Six Prefectures Hu under Kang Dai-bin rebelled; Zhiyun and Wang Jiao were sent to put them down; he was made general-in-chief of the Left Wuwei Guards, one son received an official post, and he was rewarded with a hundred gold and silver vessels and a thousand bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒於軍，贈涼州都督，錫米粟五百斛、絹帛五百段，仍令中書令張說為其碑文。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died in the army; posthumously made Military Governor of Liangzhou, granted five hundred hu of grain and five hundred lengths of silk, and Chief Minister Zhang Yue was still ordered to compose his epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died on campaign; he was posthumously made military governor of Liangzhou, granted five hundred hu of grain and five hundred bolts of silk, and Chief Minister Zhang Yue was commissioned to write his epitaph.

sentences.zh: 知運自居西陲，甚為蕃夷所憚，其後王君㚟亦號勇將，時人稱王、郭焉。

translations.literal: From the time Zhiyun held the western frontier, he was greatly feared by the various tribes; afterward Wang Jun was also styled a fierce general, and men of the time spoke of Wang and Guo together.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhiyun held the western frontier, the frontier tribes feared him greatly; later Wang Jun too was hailed as a fierce commander, and contemporaries paired the names Wang and Guo.

sentences.zh: 子英傑、英乂。

translations.literal: His sons were Yingjie and Yingyi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yingjie and Yingyi.

sentences.zh: 英傑官至左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Yingjie reached office as General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjie rose to the rank of general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 開元二十一年，幽州長史薛楚玉遣英傑及裨將吳克勤、烏知義、羅守忠等率精騎萬人及降奚之眾以討契丹，屯兵於榆關之外；

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 21, Youzhou Chief Administrator Xue Chuyu sent Yingjie and deputy generals Wu Keqin, Wu Zhiyi, Luo Shouzhong, and others to lead ten thousand elite cavalry and the masses of surrendered Xi to attack the Khitan, encamping troops beyond Yuguan Pass;
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 21, Xue Chuyu, chief administrator of Youzhou, sent Yingjie with deputies Wu Keqin, Wu Zhiyi, Luo Shouzhong, and others at the head of ten thousand elite horsemen and surrendered Xi forces against the Khitan, encamped beyond Yuguan Pass;

sentences.zh: 契丹首領可突幹引突厥之眾拒戰於都山之下。

translations.literal: The Khitan leader Ketuhan led Turk forces to resist battle beneath Mount Du.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan leader Ketuhan brought Turk forces to meet them at the foot of Mount Du.

sentences.zh: 官軍不利，知義、守忠率麾下便道遁歸。

translations.literal: The government army fared ill; Zhiyi and Shouzhong led their subordinates by a convenient route in flight and return.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial force fared badly; Zhiyi and Shouzhong took their men and fled by a side road.

sentences.zh: 英傑與克勤逢賊力戰，皆沒於陣。

translations.literal: Yingjie and Keqin met the enemy and fought fiercely; both perished in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjie and Keqin met the enemy and fought to the end; both fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 其下精銳六千餘人仍與賊苦戰，賊以英傑之首示之，竟不降，盡為賊所殺。

translations.literal: More than six thousand elite troops under them still bitterly fought the enemy; the enemy displayed Yingjie's head to them, yet they would not surrender in the end and were all killed by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: More than six thousand of their elite troops kept fighting; the enemy held up Yingjie's head, yet they would not yield and were slaughtered to the last man.

sentences.zh: 英乂，劍南西川節度使，自有傳。

translations.literal: Yingyi, Military Governor of Jiannan West Circuit, has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyi, military governor of Jiannan West Circuit, has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 王君㚟，瓜州常樂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jun was a man of Changle in Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun was a native of Changle in Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 初，為郭知運別奏，驍勇善騎射，以戰功累除右衛副率。

translations.literal: At first he was a separate memorial appointee of Guo Zhiyun, fierce and brave and skilled in mounted archery; through military achievements he was repeatedly promoted to Deputy Commander of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as a personal appointee of Guo Zhiyun, a daring rider and archer who rose through battle honors to deputy commander of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 及知運卒，遂代知運為河西、隴右節度使，遷右羽林軍將軍，判涼州都督事。

translations.literal: When Zhiyun died, he then replaced Zhiyun as Military Governor of Hexi and Longyou, was transferred to General of the Right Yulin Army, and adjudicated the affairs of Military Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhiyun's death he succeeded him as military governor of Hexi and Longyou, became general of the Right Yulin Army, and took charge of Liangzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 開元十六年冬，吐蕃大將悉諾邏率眾入寇大斗谷，又移攻甘州，焚燒市裏而去。

translations.literal: In winter of Kaiyuan 16, the Tibetan general Sinolu led masses to invade Dadou Valley, then shifted to attack Ganzhou, burned the market wards, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Kaiyuan 16 the Tibetan general Sinolu invaded Dadou Valley, then turned on Ganzhou, burned the market quarter, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 君㚟以其兵疲，整士馬以掩其後。

translations.literal: Jun, because their troops were weary, arrayed soldiers and horses to strike their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the enemy spent, Jun mustered his men and horses to strike from behind.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，賊徒凍死者甚眾，賊遂取積石軍西路而還。

translations.literal: It happened that heavy snow fell; very many of the rebels froze to death, and the rebels then took the western route of Jishi Army and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell, and great numbers of the enemy froze to death; they then retreated by the western road past Jishi Army.

sentences.zh: 君㚟令副使馬元慶、裨將車蒙追之，不及。

translations.literal: Jun ordered Deputy Commissioner Ma Yuanqing and Deputy General Che Meng to pursue them but they did not overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent his deputy Ma Yuanqing and subordinate Che Meng in pursuit, but they could not catch up.

sentences.zh: 君㚟先令人潛入賊境，於歸路燒草。

translations.literal: Jun had first sent men to infiltrate the enemy territory and burn the grass on the return route.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had already sent agents into enemy country to burn the grass along their line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 悉諾邏還至大非川，將息甲牧馬，而野草皆盡，馬死過半。

translations.literal: When Sinolu returned to Dafei River, about to rest armor and pasture horses, yet the wild grass was all gone and more than half the horses died.
translations.idiomatic: When Sinolu reached the Dafei River to rest his men and graze his horses, the pasture was gone and more than half his mounts perished.

sentences.zh: 君㚟襲其後，入至青海之西，時海水冰合，君㚟與秦州都督張景順等率將士並乘冰而渡。

translations.literal: Jun struck their rear, entering west of Qinghai; at that time the sea waters were frozen together, and Jun with Military Governor of Qinzhou Zhang Jingshun and others led officers and soldiers all to ride the ice in crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Jun struck from behind, pushing west of Qinghai; the lake had frozen over, and Jun with Zhang Jingshun, military governor of Qinzhou, and others led their troops across the ice.

sentences.zh: 會悉諾邏已度大非山，輜重及疲兵尚在青海之側，君㚟縱兵盡俘獲之，及羊馬萬數。

translations.literal: It happened that Sinolu had already crossed Mount Dafei; baggage trains and weary troops were still on the Qinghai shore, and Jun released troops who captured them all, along with sheep and horses numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Sinolu had already crossed Mount Dafei, but his baggage and exhausted troops were still by Qinghai; Jun's men took them all, along with tens of thousands of sheep and horses.

sentences.zh: 君㚟以功遷右羽林軍大將軍，攝御史中丞，依舊判涼州都督，封晉昌伯。

translations.literal: For his achievement Jun was transferred to Grand General of the Right Yulin Army, Acting Vice Censor-in-Chief, still adjudicating Military Governor of Liangzhou, and enfeoffed as Baron of Jinchang.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat Jun was made grand general of the Right Yulin Army and acting vice censor-in-chief, retained charge of Liangzhou, and enfeoffed as baron of Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 拜其父壽為少府監，仍聽致仕。

translations.literal: His father Shou was appointed Director of the Palace Workshop, and he was still permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shou was made director of the palace workshops and allowed to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 上又嘗於廣達樓引君㚟及妻夏氏設宴，賜以金帛。

translations.literal: The Emperor also once at Guangda Tower drew Jun and his wife the Lady Xia to a banquet and bestowed gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once entertained Jun and his wife Lady Xia at Guangda Tower and rewarded them with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 夏氏亦有戰功，故特賞之，封為武威郡夫人。

translations.literal: The Lady Xia also had military achievements, and therefore was specially rewarded and enfeoffed as Lady of Wuwei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xia too had earned merit in battle, and was specially honored with the title lady of Wuwei commandery.

sentences.zh: 其冬，吐蕃寇陷瓜州，執刺史田仁獻及君㚟父壽，殺掠人戶，並取軍資及倉糧。

translations.literal: That winter the Tibetans raided and captured Guazhou, seized Prefect Tian Renxian and Jun's father Shou, killed and plundered households, and also took military stores and granary grain.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Tibetans overran Guazhou, seized prefect Tian Renxian and Jun's father Shou, slaughtered and plundered the populace, and carried off military stores and granary grain.

sentences.zh: 又進攻玉門軍及常樂縣。

translations.literal: They also advanced to attack Yumen Army and Changle County.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on against Yumen Army and Changle county.

sentences.zh: 仍縱僧徒使歸涼州，謂君㚟曰：「將軍常欲以忠勇報國，今日何不一戰？」

translations.literal: They still released Buddhist monks to return to Liangzhou, saying to Jun: "General, you always wished to repay the state with loyalty and courage—why not fight one battle today?"
translations.idiomatic: They even sent monks back to Liangzhou with a message for Jun: "You always vowed to repay the realm with loyalty and courage—why not fight today?"

sentences.zh: 君㚟聞父被執，登陴西向而哭，竟不敢出兵。

translations.literal: When Jun heard his father had been seized, he ascended the ramparts, faced west, and wept, yet in the end dared not send out troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing his father was captive, Jun climbed the walls, faced west, and wept, but in the end he dared not march out.

sentences.zh: 初，涼州界有回紇、契苾、思結、渾四部落，代為酋長，君㚟微時往來涼府，為回紇等所輕。

translations.literal: At first within Liangzhou's borders were the four tribes of Uyghur, Qibi, Sijie, and Hun, each generation having its chieftain; when Jun was still obscure he came and went at Liang Prefecture and was looked down on by the Uyghurs and others.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, four tribes—the Uyghurs, Qibi, Sijie, and Hun—had long held sway as chiefs in the Liangzhou region; in his youth Jun had frequented the prefectural seat and was despised by the Uyghurs and the rest.

sentences.zh: 及君㚟為河西節度使，回紇等怏怏，恥在其麾下。

translations.literal: When Jun became Military Governor of Hexi, the Uyghurs and others were resentful, ashamed to be under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun became military governor of Hexi, the Uyghurs and others were discontent, ashamed to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 君㚟以法繩之，回紇等積怨，密使人詣東都自陳枉狀。

translations.literal: Jun restrained them by law; the Uyghurs and others accumulated resentment and secretly sent men to the Eastern Capital to state their grievances of injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Jun held them strictly to the law; their resentment grew, and they secretly sent envoys to the eastern capital to plead their case.

sentences.zh: 君㚟遽發驛奏「回紇部落難制，潛有叛謀。」

translations.literal: Jun hastily sent a relay memorial stating: "The Uyghur tribes are hard to control and secretly harbor plans of rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Jun at once sent an urgent memorial by relay: "The Uyghur tribes are unruly and secretly plot rebellion."

sentences.zh: 上使中使往按問之，回紇等竟不得理。

translations.literal: The emperor sent palace envoys to investigate and question them; in the end the Uyghurs gained no justification.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched court envoys to investigate the matter, but the Uyghurs never obtained satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 由是瀚海大都督回紇承宗長流瀼州，渾大德長流吉州，賀蘭都督契苾承明長流藤州，盧山都督思結歸國長流瓊州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huihe Chengzong, Great Governor of Hanhai, was exiled for life to Rang Prefecture; Hun Dade to Ji Prefecture; Qibi Chengming, Governor of Helan, to Teng Prefecture; and Sijie Guiguo, Governor of Lushan, to Qiong Prefecture for life.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, Huihe Chengzong, Great Governor of Hanhai, was exiled for life to Rang Prefecture; Hun Dade to Ji; Qibi Chengming, Governor of Helan, to Teng; and Sijie Guiguo, Governor of Lushan, to Qiong.

sentences.zh: 右散騎常侍李令問、特進契苾嵩以與回紇等結婚，貶令問為撫州別駕，嵩為連州別駕。

translations.literal: Right Regular Attendant of the Casual Cavalry Li Lingwen and the specially advanced Qibi Song, for having married into the Uyghur families, were demoted—Lingwen to Assistant Prefect of Fu and Song to Assistant Prefect of Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lingwen, Right Regular Attendant of the Casual Cavalry, and Qibi Song, holder of special advancement, had married into Uyghur families; Lingwen was demoted to assistant prefect of Fu and Song to assistant prefect of Lian.

sentences.zh: 於是承宗之黨瀚海州司馬護輸糾合黨與，謀殺君㚟，以復其怨。

translations.literal: Then Chengzong's faction, Hu Yuan, Military Assistant of Hanhai Prefecture, gathered accomplices and plotted to kill Wang Jun to avenge their grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong's followers then rallied around Hu Yuan, military assistant of Hanhai Prefecture, who mustered allies to kill Wang Jun and settle old scores.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃使間道往突厥，君㚟率精騎往肅州掩之，還至甘州南鞏幰驛，護輸伏兵突起，奪君㚟旌節，先殺其左右宗貞，剖其心，雲是其始謀也。

translations.literal: It happened that a Tibetan envoy was traveling by a secret route to the Turks; Jun led picked cavalry to intercept him at Suzhou. On his return, when he reached the Gongqian Post south of Gan Prefecture, Hu Yuan's hidden troops suddenly rose, seized Jun's banners and credentials, and first killed his attendant Zong Zhen, cutting out his heart and saying he had been the original plotter.
translations.idiomatic: When a Tibetan envoy took a back route toward the Turks, Jun led elite horsemen from Suzhou to ambush him. On the return march, at the Gongqian post south of Ganzhou, Hu Yuan's ambush struck: they seized Jun's command insignia, slew his aide Zong Zhen first, cut out his heart, and declared him the mastermind.

sentences.zh: 君㚟從數十人與賊力戰，自朝至晡，左右盡死。

translations.literal: Jun with several dozen followers fought the rebels fiercely from morning until afternoon; all his attendants perished.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and a few dozen men fought the rebels from morning until midafternoon until every man at his side was dead.

sentences.zh: 遂殺君㚟，馱其屍以奔吐蕃。

translations.literal: They then killed Jun, loaded his corpse on a pack animal, and fled toward Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Jun, lashed his body to a pack animal, and rode for Tibet.

sentences.zh: 追及之，護輸遂棄君㚟屍而走。

translations.literal: When pursuers caught up, Hu Yuan abandoned Jun's corpse and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers overtook them; Hu Yuan abandoned Jun's body and escaped.

sentences.zh: 上甚痛惜之，制贈特進、荊州大都督，給靈輿遞歸京師，葬於京城之東，官供喪事。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved deeply, ordered posthumous promotion to Special Advancement and Great Governor of Jingzhou, provided an imperial hearse to convey the body back to the capital, burial east of the capital, and official provision for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply, posthumously ennobling him as Special Advancement and Great Governor of Jingzhou, sending an imperial catafalque to bring his remains to Chang'an, burying him east of the city with state funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 仍令張說為其碑文，上自書石以寵異之。

translations.literal: He also had Zhang Yue compose his tomb inscription, and the emperor himself wrote it on stone as a mark of special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue was commissioned to write the epitaph, and the emperor inscribed the stone himself as an extraordinary honor.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃之寇瓜州也，分遣副將莽布支攻常樂縣，縣令賈師順嬰城固守。

translations.literal: When Tibet raided Guazhou, they separately sent the deputy general Mangbuzhi to attack Changle County; the magistrate Jia Shishun closed the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tibetan assault on Guazhou, a deputy commander named Mangbuzhi was sent against Changle, where Magistrate Jia Shishun barred the gates and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 及瓜州城陷，大將悉諾邏又盡引其眾乘勢以攻之，數日不陷。

translations.literal: When Guazhou fell, the great general Sinolu again led all his forces to press the attack by momentum; for several days they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: After Guazhou fell, the general Sinolu brought his full strength to bear on Changle, yet the county held for days.

sentences.zh: 賊中有分得漢口為妻者，其妻弟在常樂城中，悉諾邏使夜就城下詐為私見，謂師順曰：「瓜州已破，吐蕃盡眾來此，豈有拒守之理？

translations.literal: Among the rebels was one who had taken a Han woman as wife; her younger brother was in Changle. Sinolu sent him by night to the foot of the wall feigning a private meeting, saying to Shishun: "Guazhou is already taken; Tibet has brought its entire force here—how can there be reason to resist and hold out?
translations.idiomatic: One rebel had married a Han woman whose brother was inside Changle. Sinolu sent the man at night to the wall under pretense of a private visit, telling Shishun: "Guazhou is lost and the whole Tibetan army is here—what sense is there in holding out?

sentences.zh: 小人妻弟在城，情有所念，明府何不早降，以全城中之眾。」

translations.literal: This petty man's wife's brother is in the city and his feelings are bound; why does Your Honor not surrender early to preserve all within the walls?"
translations.idiomatic: My brother-in-law is in your city, and I care for him—why not surrender now and save everyone inside?"

sentences.zh: 師順答曰：「漢法，降賊者九族為戮，吾受國官爵，祗可以死拒寇，豈得背恩降賊！」

translations.literal: Shishun replied: "By Han law, one who surrenders to bandits has nine kindreds put to death. I have received rank and salary from the state; I can only resist the enemy unto death—how could I betray grace and surrender to bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: Shishun answered: "Han law condemns surrender to the death of one's entire clan. The state has honored me with office; I can only die resisting invaders—I will never betray my sovereign by yielding to rebels!"

sentences.zh: 悉諾邏知師順不降，又攻城八日，復令前使謂師順曰：「明府既不肯降，吾眾欲還，城中豈無財物以相贈耶？」

translations.literal: Knowing Shishun would not surrender, Sinolu attacked another eight days, then again sent the former envoy to tell Shishun: "Since Your Honor refuses to surrender, our host wishes to withdraw—is there nothing of value in the city you might give us?"
translations.idiomatic: When Sinolu saw Shishun would not yield, he besieged the city eight days longer, then sent the same envoy: "If you will not surrender, we mean to leave—haven't you some goods to send us on our way?"

sentences.zh: 師順請脫士卒衣裳以為賂。

translations.literal: Shishun asked to strip the soldiers' garments as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Shishun offered to hand over the soldiers' clothing as a gift.

sentences.zh: 悉諾邏知城中無財帛，夜燒死人，收營而去，引眾毀瓜州城。

translations.literal: Sinolu, knowing the city had no wealth or silk, burned the dead by night, broke camp and left, and led his forces to destroy Guazhou's walls.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the town held no treasure, Sinolu burned their corpses that night, withdrew, and marched his men to wreck Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 師順遽開門收器械，更修守備。

translations.literal: Shishun swiftly opened the gates, gathered weapons, and renewed defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Shishun at once opened the gates, collected arms, and strengthened the defenses anew.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃果使精騎回襲，而巡城知有備，始去。

translations.literal: Tibet indeed sent picked cavalry to raid back, but circling the walls they saw preparations and only then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetans did send elite horsemen back, but seeing the city ready, they circled the walls and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賈師順者，岐州人也。

translations.literal: Jia Shishun was a man of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Shishun was a native of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 以守城之功，累遷鄯州都督、隴右節度使。

translations.literal: For his merit in defending the city, he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Shanzhou and Military Commissioner of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: His defense earned repeated promotions—to Governor of Shanzhou and Military Commissioner of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 入為左領軍將軍，病卒。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as General of the Left Victorious Army and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as general of the Left Victorious Army and died in office of illness.

sentences.zh: 張守珪，陜州河北人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shougui was a man of Hebei in Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shougui came from the Hebei district of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初以戰功授平樂府別駕，從郭虔瓘於北庭鎮，遣守珪率眾救援，在路逢賊甚眾，守珪身先士卒，與之苦戰，斬首千餘級，生擒賊率頡斤一人。

translations.literal: At first for military merit he was appointed Assistant of Pingyao Prefecture; following Guo Qianguan at Beiting Fort, Qianguan sent Shougui to lead troops to the rescue. On the road they met a very large band of enemies; Shougui took the lead before the soldiers and fought bitterly, beheading more than a thousand and capturing alive one enemy leader, an Erkin.
translations.idiomatic: He first won appointment as vice-prefect of Pingyao for battlefield merit. With Guo Qianguan at Beiting, he was sent to relieve a threatened force; on the march he met a large enemy body, led the charge, fought fiercely, took more than a thousand heads, and captured an enemy chieftain called Erkin alive.

sentences.zh: 開元初，突厥又寇北庭，虔瓘令守珪間道入京奏事，守珪因上書陳利害，請引兵自蒲昌、輪臺翼而擊之。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, the Turks again raided Beiting; Qianguan ordered Shougui by a secret route to enter the capital and report affairs. Shougui therefore submitted a memorial stating advantages and harms, requesting to lead troops from Puchang and Luntai in a flanking strike.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era the Turks raided Beiting again. Qianguan sent Shougui to the capital by a hidden route with a report; there Shougui memorialized the court on strategy, asking to strike from Puchang and Luntai in a flanking attack.

sentences.zh: 及賊敗，守珪以功特加遊擊將軍，再轉幽州良社府果毅。

translations.literal: When the bandits were defeated, Shougui for his merit was specially promoted to Mobile General and twice transferred to Guoyi of Youzhou Liangsheafu.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy was beaten, he was specially promoted to mobile corps general and later transferred twice to serve as a militia commander in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 守珪儀形瑰壯，善騎射，性慷慨，有節義。

translations.literal: Shougui's bearing was magnificent and sturdy; he excelled at riding and archery, was generous by nature, and possessed integrity and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui was imposing in stature, skilled in horsemanship and archery, generous, and firm in honor.

sentences.zh: 時盧齊卿為幽州刺史，深禮遇之，常共榻而坐，謂曰：「足下數年外必節度幽、涼，為國之良將，方以子孫相托，豈得以僚屬常禮相期耶！」

translations.literal: At the time Lu Qiqing was Governor of Youzhou and treated him with deep courtesy, often sharing a couch to sit, saying to him: "Within a few years you will surely be Military Commissioner of You and Liang, a fine general of the state—I intend to entrust you with my sons and grandsons; how can we expect each other with the usual courtesy between superior and subordinate!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qiqing, then prefect of Youzhou, treated him with great respect and often sat with him on the same couch, saying: "In a few years you will command You and Liang—a pillar general of the empire. I mean to commend my descendants to you; why should we observe mere staff etiquette?"

sentences.zh: 守珪後累轉左金吾員外將軍，為建康軍使。

translations.literal: Shougui later accumulated transfers to become Left Jinwu Staff General and Military Commissioner of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts to Left Jinwu staff general and commissioner of the Jiankang army.

sentences.zh: 十五年，吐蕃寇陷瓜州，王君㚟死，河西恟懼。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Tibet raided and took Guazhou; Wang Jun died, and Hexi was panic-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen Tibet captured Guazhou; Wang Jun was killed, and the whole Hexi corridor trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 以守珪為瓜州刺史、墨離軍使，領餘眾修築州城。

translations.literal: Shougui was appointed Prefect of Guazhou and Commissioner of the Moli Army, leading the survivors to repair the prefectural walls.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui was made prefect of Guazhou and commander of the Moli army, tasked with rallying survivors to rebuild the city walls.

sentences.zh: 板堞才立，賊又暴至城下，城中人相顧失色，雖相率登陴，略無守禦之意。

translations.literal: The parapets had only just been set up when the enemy again suddenly appeared below the walls; the people looked at one another in dismay; though they climbed the battlements in numbers, they had scarcely any will to defend.
translations.idiomatic: The ramparts had barely been raised when raiders appeared at the gates. Faces paled in the streets; men climbed the walls in a mass, yet hardly anyone meant to fight.

sentences.zh: 守珪曰：「彼眾我寡，又創痍之後，不可以矢石相持，須以權道制之也。」

translations.literal: Shougui said: "They are many and we few, and we are fresh from wounds—we cannot contend with arrows and stones; we must control them by expedient means."
translations.idiomatic: Shougui said: "They outnumber us, and we are still bleeding from the last disaster—we cannot stand them off with stones and arrows. We must outwit them."

sentences.zh: 乃於城上置酒作樂，以會將士。

translations.literal: He thereupon set out wine on the walls and made music, gathering the officers and troops.
translations.idiomatic: He had wine and music set out on the battlements to feast his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 賊疑城中有備，竟不敢攻城而退。

translations.literal: The enemy suspected there were preparations in the city and in the end dared not attack but withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders, suspecting a trap, never assaulted the walls and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 守珪縱兵擊敗之。

translations.literal: Shougui loosed troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui then sallied and routed them.

sentences.zh: 於是修復廨宇，收合流亡，皆復舊業。

translations.literal: Thereupon he restored government buildings, gathered scattered exiles, and all returned to their former occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He restored government buildings, gathered the displaced, and brought people back to their old livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 守珪以戰功加銀青光祿大夫，仍以瓜州為都督府，以守珪為都督。

translations.literal: Shougui for military merit was advanced to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Court, and Guazhou was again made a Protectorate Prefecture with Shougui as Governor.
translations.idiomatic: For his victories he was made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Court; Guazhou was restored as a protectorate seat with Shougui as its governor.

sentences.zh: 瓜州地多沙磧，不宜稼穡，每年少雨，以雪水溉田。

translations.literal: Guazhou's land was mostly sandy desert, unsuited to grain; each year rain was scant, and fields were irrigated with meltwater.
translations.idiomatic: Guazhou was mostly desert sand, poor for crops, with little rain; fields depended on snowmelt irrigation.

sentences.zh: 至是渠堰盡為賊所毀，既地少林木，難為修葺。

translations.literal: By then the canals and dikes had all been destroyed by the enemy; since the region lacked timber, repair was difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The irrigation works had been wrecked in the fighting, and timber was scarce, so repairs were hard.

sentences.zh: 守珪設祭祈禱，經宿而山水暴至，大漂材木，塞澗而流，直至城下。

translations.literal: Shougui set up sacrifice and prayed; after one night mountains and rivers suddenly rose, floating a great mass of timber, blocking the ravines and flowing straight to below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui offered sacrifices and prayed; overnight floodwaters roared down, carrying huge drifts of timber that choked the ravines and rolled to the foot of the walls.

sentences.zh: 守珪使取充堰，於是水道復舊，州人刻石以紀其事。

translations.literal: Shougui had men take them to fill the dikes; thus the waterways were restored, and the people carved stone to record the event.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the logs used to rebuild the dikes, the canals flowed again as before, and the townspeople carved a stone to commemorate it.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷鄯州都督，仍充隴右節度。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Governor of Shanzhou, still filling Military Commissioner of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became governor of Shanzhou while continuing as military commissioner of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，轉幽州長史、兼御史中丞、營州都督、河北節度副大使，俄又加河北采訪處置使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to Chief Administrator of Youzhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, Governor of Yingzhou, and Vice Commissioner of the Hebei Military Commission; soon he was also made Hebei's Investigation and Disposition Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one he became chief administrator of Youzhou, censor-in-chief, governor of Yingzhou, and deputy Hebei military commissioner, soon adding the title of Hebei investigation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先是，契丹及奚連年為邊患，契丹衙官可突幹驍勇有謀略，頗為夷人所伏。

translations.literal: Before this the Khitan and Xi had year after year been border calamities; the Khitan yamen official Ketugan was valiant and strategic and much submitted to by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: For years the Khitan and Xi had harried the frontier. A Khitan official named Ketugan was fierce, shrewd, and widely feared among the tribes.

sentences.zh: 趙含章、薛楚玉等前後為幽州長史，竟不能拒。

translations.literal: Zhao Hanzhang, Xue Chuyu, and others had in succession been Chief Administrators of Youzhou yet could not repel him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hanzhang, Xue Chuyu, and other successive chiefs at Youzhou had failed to stop him.

sentences.zh: 及守珪到官，頻出擊之，每戰皆捷。

translations.literal: When Shougui reached his post he frequently went out to strike them and was victorious in every battle.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shougui took office he attacked again and again, winning every engagement.

sentences.zh: 契丹首領屈剌與可突幹恐懼，遣使詐降。

translations.literal: The Khitan leaders Quli and Ketugan were afraid and sent envoys in a false surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan leaders Quli and Ketugan grew afraid and sent envoys feigning surrender.

sentences.zh: 守珪察知其偽，遣管記右衛騎曹王悔詣其部落就謀之。

translations.literal: Shougui perceived their deception and sent his Recorder, Right Guards Cavalry Cao Wang Hui, to their encampment to plot on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui saw through the ruse and sent his aide Wang Hui, of the Right Guards cavalry office, into their camp to work out a plan.

sentences.zh: 悔至屈剌帳，賊徒初無降意，乃移其營帳漸向西北，密遣使引突厥，將殺悔以叛。

translations.literal: When Hui reached Quli's tent the rebels at first had no thought of surrender; they shifted their camp gradually northwest, secretly sent envoys to bring the Turks, and planned to kill Hui and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: At Quli's tent the tribesmen still would not yield; they shifted camp northwest, secretly summoned the Turks, and plotted to murder Hui and revolt.

sentences.zh: 會契丹別帥李過折與可突幹爭權不葉，悔潛誘之，斬屈剌可突幹，盡誅其黨，率餘眾以降。

translations.literal: It happened that the Khitan secondary chieftain Li Guozhe disputed power with Ketugan and was not reconciled; Hui secretly won him over, beheaded Quli and Ketugan, executed all their faction, and led the remaining multitude to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When a rival Khitan commander, Li Guozhe, quarreled with Ketugan, Hui secretly won him over, beheaded Quli and Ketugan, wiped out their faction, and led the survivors in surrender.

sentences.zh: 守珪因出師次於紫蒙川，大閱軍實，宴賞將士，傳屈剌、可突幹等首於東都，梟於天津橋之南。

translations.literal: Shougui therefore marched out and encamped at Zimeng River, conducted a great review of military stores, feasted and rewarded the troops, and sent the heads of Quli, Ketugan, and the like to the Eastern Capital; they were exposed south of Tianjin Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui marched to the Zimeng River, held a grand review of arms, feasted his officers, and forwarded Quli's and Ketugan's heads to Luoyang, where they were displayed south of Tianjin Bridge.

sentences.zh: 詔封李過折為北平王，使統其眾，尋為可突幹餘黨所殺。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Li Guozhe as Prince of Beiping and had him rule their masses; soon he was killed by Ketugan's remaining faction.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guozhe was enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping and set over the surrendered tribes, but soon Ketugan's diehards killed him.

sentences.zh: 二十三年春，守珪詣東都獻捷，會籍田禮畢酺宴，便為守珪飲至之禮，上賦詩以褒美之。

translations.literal: In spring of the twenty-third year Shougui went to the Eastern Capital to present victory; it coincided with the end of the ceremonial plowing feast and general drinking festival; they performed for Shougui the ritual of drinking to the limit, and the emperor composed verse to praise and beautify him.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year twenty-three Shougui came to Luoyang with news of victory, arriving as the ceremonial plowing ended and the court held a grand feast. The emperor honored him with the ceremony of "drink until done" and composed verse in praise.

sentences.zh: 遂拜守珪為輔國大將軍、右羽林大將軍、兼御史大夫，餘官並如故。

translations.literal: He thereupon appointed Shougui General Who Assists the State, Great General of the Right Forest of Feathers, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief; his other offices all remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui was then made general who assists the state, great general of the Right Forest of Feathers, and censor-in-chief, his other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 仍賜雜彩一千匹及金銀器物等，與二子官，仍詔於幽州立碑以紀功賞。

translations.literal: He also bestowed a thousand bolts of mixed silks and gold and silver utensils and the like, gave offices to two sons, and still ordered a stele erected at Youzhou to record meritorious reward.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted a thousand bolts of patterned silks plus gold and silver vessels, appointed two of Shougui's sons, and ordered a monument at Youzhou to commemorate his rewards.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，守珪裨將趙堪、白真陁羅等假以守珪之命，逼平盧軍使烏知義令率騎邀叛奚餘眾於湟水之北，將踐其禾稼。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Shougui's subordinate generals Zhao Kan, Bai Zhen'etluo, and others falsely used Shougui's command to compel the Pinglu Army Commissioner Wu Zhiyi to lead cavalry and intercept the remaining rebel Xi north of Huangshui, intending to trample their grain crop.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-six his deputies Zhao Kan and Bai Zhen'etluo forged his orders and forced the Pinglu commissioner Wu Zhiyi to lead cavalry against remnant Xi north of the Huangshui, intending to trample their crops.

sentences.zh: 知義初猶固辭，真陁羅又詐稱詔命以迫之，知義不得已而行。

translations.literal: Zhiyi at first still firmly refused; Zhen'etluo again falsely claimed an imperial edict to compel him; Zhiyi had no choice but to go.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhiyi refused at first; Bai Zhen'etluo then forged an imperial edict to force him, and Zhiyi marched against his will.

sentences.zh: 及逢賊，初勝後敗，守珪隱其敗狀而妄奏克獲之功。

translations.literal: When they met the enemy, they were first victorious then defeated; Shougui concealed the defeat and falsely memorialized a merit of capture and victory.
translations.idiomatic: They met the enemy, won at first, then lost; Shougui hid the defeat and reported a false victory.

sentences.zh: 事頗泄，上令謁者牛仙童往按之。

translations.literal: The affair leaked considerably; the emperor ordered Usher Niu Xiantong to go investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread; the emperor sent the usher Niu Xiantong to investigate.

sentences.zh: 守珪厚賂仙童，遂附會其事，但歸罪於白真陁羅，逼令自縊而死。

translations.literal: Shougui bribed Xiantong heavily; he then colluded with the affair, placing guilt only on Bai Zhen'etluo and forcing him to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui bribed Xiantong heavily; the inquiry was rigged to blame only Bai Zhen'etluo, who was forced to hang himself.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，仙童事露伏法，守珪以舊功減罪，左遷括州刺史，到官無幾，疽發背而卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Xiantong's affair was exposed and he was executed by law; Shougui for old merit had his crime reduced, was demoted to Prefect of Kuozhou, and not long after reaching office a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-seven Xiantong's corruption was exposed and he was executed; Shougui's past service earned leniency—a demotion to prefect of Kuozhou—where a carbuncle on his back killed him soon after he arrived.

sentences.zh: 弟守琦，左驍衛將軍；

translations.literal: His younger brother Shouqi was General of the Left Valiant Cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shouqi became general of the Left Valiant Cavalry;

sentences.zh: 守瑜，金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Shouyu was Jinwu General.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyu, general of the Golden Guards.

sentences.zh: 守珪子獻城、守瑜子獻恭、守琦子獻甫，三人皆為興元節度使，各自有傳。

translations.literal: Shougui's son Xiancheng, Shouyu's son Xiangong, and Shouqi's son Xianfu—the three men all became Military Commissioners of Xingyuan and each has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui's son Xiancheng, Shouyu's son Xiangong, and Shouqi's son Xianfu all became commissioners of Xingyuan; each has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 牛仙客，涇州鶉觚人也。

translations.literal: Niu Xianke was a man of Chun'guo in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Xianke was a native of Chun'guo in Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初為縣小吏，縣令傅文靜甚重之。

translations.literal: At first he was a petty clerk of the county; Magistrate Fu Wenjing esteemed him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a petty county clerk; Magistrate Fu Wenjing thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 文靜後為隴右營田使，引仙客參預其事，遂以軍功累轉洮州司馬。

translations.literal: When Wenjing later became Longyou Agricultural Colony Commissioner, he drew Xianke in to participate in those affairs; thus through military merit he was repeatedly transferred to Military Assistant of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenjing became Longyou agricultural commissioner, he brought Xianke into that work; battlefield service eventually raised him to vice-prefect of Tao.

sentences.zh: 開元初，王君㚟為河西節度使，以仙客為判官，甚委信之。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, Wang Jun was Military Commissioner of Hexi and made Xianke his judicial secretary, entrusting him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, Wang Jun as Hexi commissioner made Xianke his administrative judge and trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 時又有判官宋貞，與仙客俱為腹心之任。

translations.literal: At the time there was also judicial secretary Song Zhen; with Xianke he shared duties as trusted intimates.
translations.idiomatic: Another judge, Song Zhen, shared with Xianke the role of trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 及君㚟死，宋貞亦為回紇所殺，仙客以不從獲免。

translations.literal: When Jun died, Song Zhen was also killed by the Uyghurs; Xianke because he did not follow along was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun was killed, Song Zhen died with the Uyghur rebels; Xianke escaped because he had not joined them.

sentences.zh: 俄而蕭嵩代君㚟為河西節度，又以軍政委於仙客。

translations.literal: Soon Xiao Song replaced Jun as Hexi Military Commissioner and again entrusted military administration to Xianke.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Song soon replaced Jun as Hexi commissioner and again left military affairs in Xianke's hands.

sentences.zh: 仙客清勤不倦，接待上下，必以誠信。

translations.literal: Xianke was pure, diligent, and untiring; in receiving people above and below he always used sincerity and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke was scrupulous and tireless, treating superiors and subordinates alike with honest good faith.

sentences.zh: 及嵩入知政事，數稱薦之。

translations.literal: When Song entered to manage state affairs, he repeatedly praised and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Song entered the central government, he recommended Xianke again and again.

sentences.zh: 稍遷太仆少卿，判涼州別駕事，仍知節度留後事。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, acting as Vice Prefect of Liangzhou affairs, still knowing frontier military affairs as acting commissioner in charge of the rear post.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of the imperial stud, acting vice-prefect of Liangzhou, and still managed frontier affairs as acting rear commissioner.

sentences.zh: 竟代嵩為河西節度使，判涼州事。

translations.literal: In the end he replaced Song as Military Commissioner of Hexi, acting Liangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually succeeded Xiao Song as Hexi military commissioner, with charge of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷太仆卿、殿中監，軍使如故。

translations.literal: He passed through Minister of the Stud and Director of the Palace Armory; his military commission remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He served as minister of the stud and as palace armory director while keeping his military command.

sentences.zh: 開元二十四年秋，代信安王祎為朔方行軍大總管，右散騎常侍崔希逸代仙客知河西節度事。

translations.literal: In autumn of Kaiyuan twenty-four he replaced Prince Xin'an Li Yi as Grand General of Campaigns for Shuofang; Right Regular Attendant of the Casual Cavalry Cui Xiyi replaced Xianke in knowing Hexi military commission affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Kaiyuan twenty-four he replaced Prince Xin'an Li Yi as grand commander of the Shuofang campaign; Cui Xiyi took over Hexi from him as right regular attendant of the casual cavalry.

sentences.zh: 初，仙客在河西節度時，省用所積鉅萬，希逸以其事奏聞，上令刑部員外郎張利貞馳傳往覆視之。

translations.literal: At first, while Xianke was Military Commissioner of Hexi, he economized and accumulated tens of thousands; Xiyi memorialized this matter to inform the throne; the emperor ordered Ministry of Justice Staff Official Zhang Lizhen by rapid relay to go and re-examine it.
translations.idiomatic: While commanding Hexi, Xianke had saved enormous sums through frugality. Xiyi reported this; the emperor sent Zhang Lizhen of the Ministry of Justice posthaste to verify the accounts.

sentences.zh: 仙客所積倉庫盈滿，器械精勁，皆如希逸之狀。

translations.literal: What Xianke had accumulated—storehouses full to overflowing, weapons refined and strong—all accorded with Xiyi's report.
translations.idiomatic: Storehouses were packed and weapons in excellent order, exactly as Xiyi had described.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，以仙客為尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and made Xianke a Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and named him a minister.

sentences.zh: 中書令張九齡執奏以為不可，乃加實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling obstinately memorialized that it could not be done; he was then given two hundred households of actual enfeoffment instead.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling objected that he was unfit for such honor, so the emperor granted him two hundred supplemental estates instead.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，九齡等罷知政事，遂以仙客為工部尚書、同中書門下三品，仍知門下事。

translations.literal: That year in the eleventh month Jiuling and the others were dismissed from managing state affairs; Xianke was thereupon made Minister of Works, Fellow of the Secretariat-Chancellery Triumvir, still knowing Gate Chamberlain affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That November Jiuling fell from power; Xianke was made minister of works, coequal counselor of the third grade, and acting head of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時有監察御史周子諒竊言於御史大夫李適之曰：「牛仙客不才，濫登相位，大夫國之懿親，豈得坐觀其事？」

translations.literal: At the time Supervising Censor Zhou Ziliang secretly said to Censor-in-Chief Li Shizhi: "Niu Xianke lacks talent yet has rashly ascended the phase position; the Grandee is a treasured kinsman of the state—how can he sit and watch this affair?"
translations.idiomatic: The supervising censor Zhou Ziliang whispered to Censor-in-Chief Li Shizhi: "Niu Xianke is incompetent yet has climbed to the chancellorship. You are the emperor's kin—can you simply watch?"

sentences.zh: 適之遽奏子諒之言，上大怒，廷詰之，子諒辭窮，於朝堂決配流瀼州，行至藍田而死。

translations.literal: Shizhi hastily memorialized Ziliang's words; the emperor was furious, questioned him in court; Ziliang's words were exhausted; at court they sentenced him to exile to Rang Prefecture; on the road at Lantian he died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhi reported the remark at once. The emperor raged, interrogated Zhou at court until he had no answer, and sentenced him to exile at Rang; he died on the road at Lantian.

sentences.zh: 仙客既居相位，獨善其身，唯諾而已。

translations.literal: Once Xianke occupied the phase position, he cultivated only himself and assented—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the chancellorship, Xianke minded only his own safety and answered every question with yes.

sentences.zh: 所有錫賫，皆緘封不啟。

translations.literal: All bestowals and gifts he sealed shut without opening.
translations.idiomatic: Every gift from the throne he sealed untouched.

sentences.zh: 百司有所諮決，仙客曰：「但依令式可也』，不敢措手裁決。

translations.literal: When the hundred offices had matters for consultation and decision, Xianke said: "Just follow the regulations and statutes—that will do," and dared not lay hand to make judgments.
translations.idiomatic: When departments sought decisions, Xianke would say, "Just follow the regulations and statutes—that will do," and refused to intervene.

sentences.zh: 明年，特封豳國公，贈其父意為禮部尚書，祖會為涇州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year he was specially enfeoffed Duke of Bin; his father Yi was posthumously given Minister of Rites, his grandfather Hui Prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was specially enfeoffed as Duke of Bin; his father Yi was posthumously made minister of rites and his grandfather Hui posthumously made prefect of Jing.

sentences.zh: 俄又進拜侍中，兼兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was further promoted to Palace Attendant, concurrently Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to palace attendant and minister of war.

sentences.zh: 天寶年，改易官名，拜左相，尚書如故。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, when office names were changed, he was appointed Left Chancellor; his ministership remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When titles were reorganized in the Tianbao era, he became left chancellor while keeping his ministry.

sentences.zh: 其年七月卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: That year in the seventh month he died, age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died that seventh month at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 內出絹一千匹、布五百端，遣中使送至宅以賻之，贈尚書左丞，謚曰貞簡。

translations.literal: From within were issued a thousand bolts of silk and five hundred bolts of cloth; palace envoys were sent to his residence to present them as funeral gifts; he was posthumously given Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat and titled Zhenjian (Upright and Simple).
translations.idiomatic: The palace sent a thousand bolts of silk and five hundred of cloth by court envoy as funeral gifts; he was posthumously honored as left vice minister of the secretariat with the posthumous name Upright and Simple.

sentences.zh: 初，仙客為朔方軍使，以姚崇孫閎為判官。

translations.literal: At first when Xianke was Military Commissioner of Shuofang, he took Yao Chong's grandson Hong as judicial secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When he first commanded Shuofang, he took Yao Chong's grandson Hong as his administrative judge.

sentences.zh: 及知政事，閎累遷侍御史，自雲能通鬼道，預知休咎。

translations.literal: When he came to know state affairs, Hong was repeatedly promoted to Attending Censor; he claimed himself able to penetrate the ghostly way and foreknow fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianke entered the government, Hong rose to attending censor, claiming powers of spirit-mediumship to foresee good and ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 仙客頗信惑之。

translations.literal: Xianke was quite deluded into believing him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke came to believe him deeply.

sentences.zh: 及疾甚，閎請為仙客祈禱，在其門下，遂逼仙客令作遺表薦閎叔尚書右丞弈及兵部侍郎盧奐堪代己，閎為起草。

translations.literal: When his illness was severe, Hong requested to pray for Xianke; at his gate he pressed Xianke to make a deathbed memorial recommending Hong's uncle, Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat Yi, and Vice Minister of War Lu Huan as able to replace himself; Hong drafted it.
translations.idiomatic: In his final illness Hong offered prayers at his gate, then forced Xianke to draft a deathbed memorial naming Hong's uncle Yi, right vice minister of the secretariat, and Vice Minister Lu Huan as his successors; Hong wrote the draft.

sentences.zh: 仙客時既危殆，署字不成，其妻因中使來吊，以其表上。

translations.literal: Xianke's time was already perilously near; his signature characters would not form. His wife, because the palace envoy came to condole, presented that memorial upward.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xianke was too weak to sign clearly; when a court envoy came to mourn, his wife submitted the memorial for him.

sentences.zh: 玄宗覽而怒之，左遷弈為永陽太守，盧奐為臨淄太守，賜閎死。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong read it and was angry; Yi was demoted to Prefect of Yongyang, Lu Huan to Prefect of Linzi, and Hong was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong read the document and flew into a rage: Yi was banished to Yongyang, Lu Huan to Linzi, and Hong was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 王忠嗣，太原祁人也，家於華州之鄭縣。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongsi was a native of Qi in Taiyuan, and his family dwelt in Zheng County in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongsi was from Qi in Taiyuan; his family made their home in Zheng County, Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父海賓，太子右衛率、豐安軍使、太谷男，以驍勇聞隴上。

translations.literal: His father Haibin was Right Captain of the Crown Prince's Right Guard, commissioner of Feng'an Army, and Baron of Taigu, famed on Longxi for fierce courage.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Haibin served as Right Captain of the Crown Prince's Right Guard, commissioner of Feng'an Army, and Baron of Taigu, renowned on the northwestern frontier for his valor.

sentences.zh: 開元二年七月，吐蕃入寇，朝廷起薛訥攝左羽林將軍，為隴右防禦使，率杜賓客、郭知運、王晙、安思順以禦之，以海賓為先鋒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Kaiyuan, Tibetans raided; the court raised Xue Ne as acting Left General of the Feathered Forest, made him Longyou defense commissioner, led Du Binke, Guo Zhiyun, Wang Jun, and An Sishun to resist them, and made Haibin vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 2 (714), when Tibetans invaded, the court recalled Xue Ne as acting Left General of the Feathered Forest and appointed him Longyou defense commissioner. He led Du Binke, Guo Zhiyun, Wang Jun, and An Sishun to meet the threat, with Haibin as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 及賊於渭州西界武階驛，苦戰勝之，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: When they reached the enemy at Wujie Post on the western border of Weizhou, after bitter fighting they defeated them and killed and captured a great many.
translations.idiomatic: At Wujie Post on the western border of Weizhou they fought a fierce battle and won, inflicting heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 諸將嫉其功，按兵不救，海賓以眾寡不敵，歿於陣。

translations.literal: The generals envied his merit and held their troops back without rescuing him; Haibin, outnumbered, fell on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Other generals, jealous of his success, held their troops back and did not relieve him. Outnumbered, Haibin died in battle.

sentences.zh: 大軍乘其勢擊之，斬首一萬七千級，獲馬七萬五千匹，羊牛十四萬頭。

translations.literal: The main army followed their momentum and struck, taking seventeen thousand heads, seventy-five thousand horses, and one hundred forty thousand sheep and cattle.
translations.idiomatic: The main force pressed the advantage and routed the enemy, taking 17,000 heads, 75,000 horses, and 140,000 sheep and cattle.

sentences.zh: 玄宗聞而憐之，詔贈左金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong heard and pitied him, and by edict posthumously appointed him Left Major General of the Golden Canopy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong heard of it he was moved to pity and ordered posthumous promotion to Left Major General of the Golden Canopy.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣初名訓，年九歲，以父死王事，起復拜朝散大夫、尚輦奉禦，賜名忠嗣，養於禁中累年。

translations.literal: Zhongsi's original name was Xun; at age nine, because his father died in the service of the throne, he was recalled from mourning and appointed Court Gentleman for Imperial Entertainments and Attendant of the Imperial Carriage, granted the name Zhongsi, and raised in the Forbidden City for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi had originally been named Xun. At nine, because his father had died in imperial service, he was recalled from mourning and appointed Court Gentleman for Imperial Entertainments and Attendant of the Imperial Carriage; he was given the name Zhongsi and raised within the palace for many years.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在忠邸，與之遊處。

translations.literal: When the future Emperor Suzong lived at the Residence of Loyalty, he played and kept company with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Suzong was lodged at the Residence of Loyalty, the two of them spent their days together as companions.

sentences.zh: 及長，雄毅寡言，嚴重有武略。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was bold and taciturn, solemn and possessed of martial strategy.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he proved bold and reserved, grave in bearing and skilled in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以其兵家子，與之論兵，應對縱橫，皆出意表。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong, seeing him as the son of a military family, discussed warfare with him; his replies ranged far and wide and always exceeded expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong, knowing him for a soldier's son, would discuss strategy with him; his answers were wide-ranging and invariably beyond what anyone expected.

sentences.zh: 玄宗謂之曰：「爾後必為良將。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong told him, "You will surely become a fine general hereafter."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told him, "You are bound to become an excellent general one day."

sentences.zh: 十八年，又贈其父安西大都護。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year his father was again posthumously made Grand Protector-General of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 18 (730) his father was again posthumously promoted to Grand Protector-General of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 其後，遂從河西節度、兵部尚書蕭嵩，河東副元帥、信安王祎，並引為兵馬使。

translations.literal: Afterward he followed Hexi military governor and Minister of War Xiao Song and Hedong deputy commander-in-chief Prince Xin'an of Yi, and both took him on as army cavalry commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he served under Hexi military governor and Minister of War Xiao Song and under Hedong deputy commander-in-chief Prince Xin'an of Yi; both men appointed him army cavalry commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十一年再轉左領軍衛郎將、河西討擊副使、左威衛將軍、賜紫金魚袋、清源男，兼檢校代州都督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred again to Left Upright Guard commandant, Hexi punitive vice-commissioner, Left Awesome Guard general, granted purple-gold fish tally and the title Baron of Qingyuan, and concurrently acting inspector of Daizhou governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 21 (733) he was promoted again to commandant of the Left Upright Guard, Hexi punitive vice-commissioner, and general of the Left Awesome Guard; he received a purple-gold fish tally and the title Baron of Qingyuan, and concurrently served as acting inspector of the Daizhou governor.

sentences.zh: 嘗短皇甫惟明義弟王昱，憾焉，遂為所陷，貶東陽府左果毅。
