translations.literal: He once disparaged Huangfu Weiming's sworn brother Wang Yu; Wang bore a grudge and had him framed, and he was demoted to Left Fruithelm of Dongyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He had once spoken slightingly of Huangfu Weiming's sworn brother Wang Yu. Wang resented it and engineered his downfall, and Zhongsi was demoted to Left Fruithelm of Dongyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屬河西節度使杜希望謀拔新城，或言忠嗣之材足以輯事，必欲取勝，非其人不可。

translations.literal: When Hexi military governor Du Xiwang planned to capture Xincheng, someone said Zhongsi's talent could assemble the task and secure victory—no one else would do.
translations.idiomatic: When Hexi military governor Du Xiwang planned to take Xincheng, some argued that only Zhongsi had the ability to pull the campaign together and that victory was impossible without him.

sentences.zh: 希望即奏聞，詔追忠嗣赴河西。

translations.literal: Du Xiwang immediately memorialized; an edict recalled Zhongsi to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiwang memorialized at once, and an edict recalled Zhongsi to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 既下新城，忠嗣之功居多，因授左威衛郎將，專知行軍兵馬。

translations.literal: Once Xincheng fell, Zhongsi's merit was greatest, so he was made Left Awesome Guard commandant and put in charge of campaign horse and infantry.
translations.idiomatic: After Xincheng was taken, Zhongsi's contribution ranked first; he was appointed commandant of the Left Awesome Guard and placed in sole charge of campaign horse and infantry.

sentences.zh: 是秋，吐蕃大下，報新城之役，晨壓官軍，眾寡不敵，

translations.literal: That autumn Tibetans descended in force to avenge the Xincheng battle, pressing the government army at dawn; they were few against many.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Tibetans came down in force to avenge the battle for Xincheng. At dawn they bore down on the imperial army, which was heavily outnumbered.

sentences.zh: 師人皆懼焉。

translations.literal: The troops were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were all afraid.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣乃以所部策馬而前，左右馳突，當者無不辟易，出而復合，殺數百人，賊眾遂亂。

translations.literal: Zhongsi then led his troops charging forward on horseback, wheeling left and right in sudden rushes; none who faced him failed to give way. He broke out and rejoined, killing several hundred, and the enemy forces fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi then spurred his men forward, charging to left and right; all who met him gave way. He broke through and rallied again, killing several hundred, and the enemy ranks collapsed into confusion.

sentences.zh: 三軍翼而擊之，吐蕃大敗。

translations.literal: The three armies struck from the flanks and Tibetans were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies closed on the flanks and the Tibetans were routed.

sentences.zh: 以功最，詔拜左金吾衛將軍同正員，尋又兼左羽林軍上將軍、河東節度副使，兼大同軍使。

translations.literal: For the foremost merit, an edict appointed him Left Golden Canopy Guard general of regular rank; soon after he also held Left Feathered Forest Army senior general, Hedong deputy military governor, and commissioner of Datong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Because his merit ranked highest, he was appointed by edict Left Golden Canopy Guard general of regular rank; soon afterward he also served as senior general of the Left Feathered Forest Army, deputy military governor of Hedong, and commissioner of Datong Army.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，以本官兼代州都督，攝御史大夫，兼充河東節度，又加雲麾將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, with his current office he also served as Daizhou governor, acting censor-in-chief, and concurrently Hedong military governor, with additional title Cloud Spear General.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 28 (740), retaining his existing posts, he also served as governor of Daizhou, acting censor-in-chief, and military governor of Hedong, and was further promoted to Cloud Spear General.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，代韋光乘為朔方節度使，仍加權知河東節度事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he replaced Wei Guangcheng as Shuofang military governor, still with concurrent oversight of Hedong military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 29 (741) he replaced Wei Guangcheng as military governor of Shuofang while also holding concurrent authority over Hedong.

sentences.zh: 其月，以田仁琬充河東節度使，忠嗣依舊朔方節度。

translations.literal: That month Tian Renwan was made Hedong military governor; Zhongsi remained Shuofang military governor as before.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Tian Renwan was appointed military governor of Hedong, while Zhongsi continued as military governor of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，兼靈州都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao he was also made area commander of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 (742) he was also made area commander of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲北伐，與奚怒皆戰於桑乾河，三敗之，大虜其眾，耀武漠北，高會而旋。

translations.literal: That year he campaigned north; he fought the Xi Nujie on the Sanggan River, defeated them three times, carried off many captives, displayed martial might north of the desert, held a grand feast, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That year he marched north, fought the Xi Nujie on the Sanggan River, defeated them three times, took many captives, displayed his power in the northern desert, feasted his troops, and returned.

sentences.zh: 時突厥葉護新有內難，忠嗣盛兵磧口以威振之。

translations.literal: At the time the Turkic yabghu was newly troubled by internal conflict; Zhongsi massed troops at Qikou to overawe them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks were newly torn by internal strife, Zhongsi massed troops at Qikou to intimidate them.

sentences.zh: 烏蘇米施可汗懼而請降，竟遷延不至。

translations.literal: Qaghan Wusumishi grew afraid and requested surrender, but kept delaying and never came.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan Wusumishi grew afraid and asked to surrender, but kept delaying and never came.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣乃縱反間於拔悉密與葛邏祿、回紇三部落，攻米施可汗走之。

translations.literal: Zhongsi then sowed dissension among the Basmyl, Qarluk, and Uyghur tribes, set them against Qaghan Mishishi, and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi then set the Basmyl, Qarluk, and Uyghur tribes against one another, attacked Qaghan Mishishi, and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣因出兵伐之，取其右廂而歸，其西葉護及毗伽可敦、男殺葛臘哆率其部落千餘帳入朝，因加左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Zhongsi then led troops to attack him, took his right wing, and returned; the Western yabghu, Qaghan Bilge Kedun, and Western Shad Geladuo led more than a thousand yurts of their tribes to court, whereupon he was made Grand General of the Left Wuwei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi then marched against him, took his right wing, and withdrew; the Western yabghu, Qaghan Bilge Kedun, and Western Shad Geladuo led more than a thousand yurts of their tribes to court, and he was made grand general of the Left Wuwei Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，又再破怒皆及突厥之眾。

translations.literal: The next year he again twice defeated the Nujie and Turkic forces.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he again twice defeated the Nujie and the Turks.

sentences.zh: 自是塞外晏然，虜不敢入。

translations.literal: From then on the outer passes were tranquil and the barbarians dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the frontier was quiet and the nomads dared not raid.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載，突厥九姓拔悉密葉等竟攻殺烏蘇米施可汗，傳首京師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao, Ye of the Basmyl of the Turks' nine surnames and others attacked and killed Qaghan Wusumishi and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 3 (744), Ye of the Basmyl among the Turks' nine surnames and others attacked and killed Qaghan Wusumishi and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 四載，加攝御史大夫，充河東節度采訪使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made acting Censor-in-Chief and military commissioner and surveillance commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 4 (745) he was made acting censor-in-chief and military commissioner and surveillance commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 五月，進封清源縣公。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Qingyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was advanced in rank to Duke of Qingyuan County.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣少以勇敢自負，及居節將，以持重安邊為務。

translations.literal: Zhongsi in youth had prided himself on bravery; once a frontier commander he made steadiness and pacifying the border his task.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Zhongsi had prided himself on courage, but once he held a frontier command he made steadiness and securing the border his chief concern.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂人云：「國家昇平之時，為將者在撫其眾而已。

translations.literal: He once told others, "When the state is at peace, a general need only comfort his troops.
translations.idiomatic: He once remarked, "In times when the empire is at peace, all a general need do is look after his men.

sentences.zh: 吾不欲疲中國之力，以僥功名耳。」

translations.literal: I do not wish to exhaust the strength of the Middle Kingdom to grasp at merit."
translations.idiomatic: I have no wish to wear down the empire's strength merely to snatch at glory."

sentences.zh: 但訓練士馬，缺則補之。

translations.literal: He only trained soldiers and horses, replenishing whenever there was a shortage.
translations.idiomatic: He confined himself to drilling troops and horses and filling any shortfall.

sentences.zh: 有漆弓百五十斤，嘗貯之袋中，示無所用。

translations.literal: He owned a lacquered bow of one hundred fifty jin; he often stored it in a bag to show it was unused.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed a lacquered bow weighing a hundred and fifty jin, which he would keep stowed in a bag to show he had no use for it.

sentences.zh: 軍中皆日夜思戰，因多縱間諜以伺虜之隙，時以奇兵襲之，故士樂為用，師出必勝。

translations.literal: The army all yearned day and night for battle; he sent many spies to watch for barbarian gaps and struck with unexpected troops, so soldiers were glad to serve and campaigns invariably won.
translations.idiomatic: His men burned day and night to fight; he sent out many spies to catch the enemy off guard and struck with surprise detachments, so the troops were eager to follow him and his campaigns invariably succeeded.

sentences.zh: 每軍出，即各召本將付其兵器，令給士卒，雖一弓一箭，必書其名姓於上以記之，軍罷卻納。

translations.literal: Each time the army marched out he summoned each commander and handed over weapons, ordering distribution to the soldiers—even one bow or one arrow had the bearer's name written on it for record, and after the campaign they were returned.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the army took the field he summoned each commander, issued weapons, and ordered them distributed to the men; even a single bow or arrow had the soldier's name inscribed upon it, and after the campaign everything was turned back in.

sentences.zh: 若遺失，即驗其名罪之。

translations.literal: If anything was lost, the name was checked and the guilty one punished.
translations.idiomatic: If anything was lost, the name on it was traced and the offender punished.

sentences.zh: 故人人自勸，甲仗充牣矣。

translations.literal: Thus everyone urged himself on, and armor and weapons filled the storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: Thus every man drove himself on, and the armories overflowed with arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 四載，又兼河東節度采訪使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he also held Hedong investigative commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 4 (745) he was also made investigative commissioner for the Hedong circuit.

sentences.zh: 自朔方至雲中，緣邊數千里，當要害地開拓舊城，或自創制，斥地各數百里。

translations.literal: From Shuofang to Yunzhong, along the border for several thousand li, at strategic points he reopened old cities or built new ones, extending territory hundreds of li in each case.
translations.idiomatic: From Shuofang to Yunzhong, along thousands of li of frontier, he reopened abandoned fortresses at key points or built new ones, pushing the border outward by hundreds of li in each sector.

sentences.zh: 自張仁亶之後四十餘年，忠嗣繼之，北塞之人，復罷戰矣。

translations.literal: More than forty years after Zhang Renzan, Zhongsi continued this work, and the people of the northern frontier ceased fighting again.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty years after Zhang Renzan, Zhongsi took up the same work, and the peoples of the northern marches again laid down their arms.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，河隴以皇甫惟明敗衄之後，因忠嗣以持節充西平郡太守，判武威郡事，充河西、隴右節度使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, after Huangfu Weiming's defeat, He-Long posted Zhongsi with credential as Xiping prefect, acting Wuwei prefect, and Hexi-Longyou military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianbao 5 (746), after Huangfu Weiming's defeat on the He-Long frontier, Zhongsi was sent with imperial credential as prefect of Xiping, acting prefect of Wuwei, and military governor of Hexi and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 其月，又權知朔方、河東節度使事。

translations.literal: That month he also held oversight of Shuofang and Hedong military governor affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he was also given concurrent authority over Shuofang and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣佩四將印，控制萬里，勁兵重鎮，皆歸掌握，自國初已來，未之有也。

translations.literal: Zhongsi bore four general seals, commanding ten thousand li; crack troops and key garrisons all fell under his grasp—unprecedented since the founding of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi wore four general's seals and controlled a frontier ten thousand li across; crack troops and strategic strongholds all lay in his hands—something without precedent since the dynasty's founding.

sentences.zh: 尋遷鴻臚卿，餘如故，又加金紫光祿大夫，仍授一子五品官。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Court of State Ceremonial while his other offices remained; he was also made Grand Master of Splendid Honors with Golden Seal, and one son was granted a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial while retaining his other posts; he was further promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Honors with Golden Seal, and one of his sons was granted a fifth-rank office.

sentences.zh: 後頻戰青海、積石，皆大克捷。

translations.literal: Later he fought repeatedly at Qinghai and Jishi, all great victories.
translations.idiomatic: He later fought repeatedly around Qinghai and Jishi, winning resounding victories each time.

sentences.zh: 尋又伐吐谷渾於墨離，虜其全國而歸。

translations.literal: Soon he attacked the Tuyuhun at Moli and took their entire state captive back.
translations.idiomatic: He soon campaigned against the Tuyuhun at Moli and brought their entire people back as captives.

sentences.zh: 初，忠嗣在河東、朔方日久，備諳邊事，得士卒心。

translations.literal: At first, having long been in Hedong and Shuofang, he thoroughly knew border affairs and won the hearts of the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At first, after long service in Hedong and Shuofang, he knew the frontier inside out and had won his soldiers' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及至河、隴，頗不習其物情，又以功名富貴自處，望減於往日矣。

translations.literal: When he reached He-Long he was less attuned to local conditions, and he treated himself with rank and wealth; his standing fell from before.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the He-Long commands he was less familiar with local conditions, and he carried himself as a man of rank and fortune; his reputation declined from what it had been.

sentences.zh: 其載四月，固讓朔方、河東節度，許之。

translations.literal: That fourth month he firmly declined Shuofang and Hedong commands; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of that year he firmly declined the Shuofang and Hedong commands, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 玄宗方事石堡城，詔問以攻取之略，忠嗣奏云：「石堡險固，吐蕃舉國而守之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was set on Shibao Fortress and asked strategy for taking it; Zhongsi memorialized, "Shibao is perilous and solid; Tibet holds it with the whole state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was bent on taking Shibao Fortress and asked Zhongsi for a plan of attack. Zhongsi memorialized: "Shibao is steep and strongly fortified; the Tibetans defend it with the full strength of their state.

sentences.zh: 若頓兵堅城之下，必死者數萬，然後事可圖也。

translations.literal: If troops are stationed beneath that strong wall, tens of thousands must die before the affair can be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: If we camp our army beneath those walls, tens of thousands will have to die before the thing can be done.

sentences.zh: 臣恐所得不如所失，請休兵秣馬，觀釁而取之，計之上者。」

translations.literal: Your servant fears the gain will not match the loss; please rest the troops and feed the horses, watch for a breach and take it—that is the highest plan."
translations.idiomatic: I fear what we gain will not repay what we lose. Let the army rest and the horses feed, watch for an opening, and strike then—that is the wisest course."

sentences.zh: 玄宗因不快。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was displeased because of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 李林甫尤忌忠嗣，日求其過。

translations.literal: Li Linfu especially envied Zhongsi and daily sought his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu harbored a special hatred for Zhongsi and looked daily for grounds against him.

sentences.zh: 六載，會董延光獻策請下石堡城，詔忠嗣分兵應接之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when Dong Yanguang offered a plan to take Shibao Fortress, an edict ordered Zhongsi to divide troops to support him.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 6 (747), when Dong Yanguang proposed a plan to capture Shibao Fortress, an edict ordered Zhongsi to detach troops to support the operation.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣僶俯而從，延光不悅。

translations.literal: Zhongsi bowed submissively and complied; Yanguang was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi bowed and submitted, but Yanguang was not satisfied.

sentences.zh: 河西兵馬使李光弼危之，遽而入告。

translations.literal: Hexi army commissioner Li Guangbi saw the danger and rushed in to report.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi army commissioner Li Guangbi saw the peril and hurried in to warn him.

sentences.zh: 將及於庭，忠嗣曰：「李將軍有何事乎？」

translations.literal: When he was about to reach the hall, Zhongsi said, "General Li, what business do you have?"
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to enter the hall, Zhongsi called out, "General Li—what brings you?"

sentences.zh: 光弼進而言曰：「請議軍。」

translations.literal: Guangbi advanced and said, "I request to discuss the army."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi stepped forward and said, "I wish to discuss the army."

sentences.zh: 忠嗣曰：「何也？」

translations.literal: Zhongsi said, "What for?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi asked, "What about it?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「向者大夫以士卒為心，有拒董延光之色，雖曰受詔，實奪其謀。

translations.literal: He replied, "Just now, my lord, you took the soldiers' hearts and showed refusal of Dong Yanguang; though you said you accepted the edict, in truth you thwarted his plan.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "A moment ago you put the troops' welfare first and showed you meant to resist Dong Yanguang. Though you said you obeyed the edict, in fact you blocked his plan.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 大夫以數萬眾付之，而不懸重賞，則何以賈三軍之勇乎？

translations.literal: My lord entrusted him with tens of thousands yet hung no heavy reward—how then buy the three armies' courage?
translations.idiomatic: You placed tens of thousands of men in his hands yet offered no rich reward—how can you expect to stir the army's fighting spirit?

sentences.zh: 大夫財帛盈庫，何惜數萬段之賞以杜其讒口乎！

translations.literal: My lord's treasury overflows with goods—why spare tens of thousands in silk rewards to silence his slanderous mouth?
translations.idiomatic: Your storehouses overflow with goods—why not spend a few ten-thousands in rewards to shut his mouth before he slanders you?

sentences.zh: 彼如不捷，歸罪於大夫矣。」

translations.literal: If he does not succeed, blame will return upon my lord."
translations.idiomatic: If he fails, the blame will fall on you."

sentences.zh: 忠嗣曰：「李將軍，忠嗣計已決矣。

translations.literal: Zhongsi said, "General Li, Zhongsi's mind is already settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi said, "General Li, my mind is made up.

sentences.zh: 平生始望，豈及貴乎？

translations.literal: My life's first hope—how could it reach nobility?
translations.idiomatic: What I hoped for in life—how did that ever extend to rank and riches?

sentences.zh: 今爭一城，得之未制於敵，不得之未害於國，忠嗣豈以數萬人之命易一官哉？

translations.literal: Now contesting one fortress—taking it does not control the foe, not taking it does not harm the state—would Zhongsi trade tens of thousands of lives for one office?
translations.idiomatic: Now we fight over one fortress: taking it does not bring the enemy to heel, and failing to take it does not harm the state. Would I trade tens of thousands of lives for a single promotion?

sentences.zh: 假如明主見責，豈失一金吾羽林將軍，歸朝宿衛乎！

translations.literal: Suppose the enlightened sovereign blames me—would I not merely lose a Golden Canopy or Feathered Forest general and return to palace guard?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose the enlightened sovereign rebukes me—at worst I lose a post as Golden Canopy or Feathered Forest general and return to guard the palace at court.

sentences.zh: 其次，豈失一黔中上佐乎？

translations.literal: Next, would I not merely lose a chief assistant post in Qianzhong?
translations.idiomatic: After that, at worst I lose a chief aide's post in Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 此所甘心也。

translations.literal: That I could accept with ease.
translations.idiomatic: I could accept that willingly.

sentences.zh: 雖然，公實愛我。」

translations.literal: Even so, you truly care for me."
translations.idiomatic: Even so—you truly care for me."

sentences.zh: 光弼謝曰：「向者恐累大夫，敢以衷告。

translations.literal: Guangbi apologized, "Just now I feared burdening my lord and ventured to speak my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi apologized: "I feared I might bring trouble on you and ventured to speak from the heart.

sentences.zh: 大夫能行古人之事，非光弼所及也。」

translations.literal: My lord can do what the ancients did—I cannot match you."
translations.idiomatic: You are capable of what the ancients did; I am not your equal."

sentences.zh: 遂趨而出。

translations.literal: He hurried out at once.
translations.idiomatic: With that he hurried out.

sentences.zh: 及延光過期不克，訴忠嗣緩師，故師出無功。

translations.literal: When Yanguang passed the deadline without success he accused Zhongsi of slowing the army, so the campaign achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanguang passed his deadline without success he accused Zhongsi of dragging his feet, and the expedition came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 李林甫又令濟陽別駕魏林告忠嗣，稱往任朔州刺史，忠嗣為河東節度，雲「早與忠王同養宮中，我欲尊奉太子。」

translations.literal: Li Linfu also had Jiyang assistant prefect Wei Lin accuse Zhongsi, claiming that when Lin had been Shuozhou prefect and Zhongsi Hedong military governor, he said, "I was raised in the palace early with the Loyal Prince; I wish to honor and support the Crown Prince."
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu also had Jiyang assistant prefect Wei Lin denounce Zhongsi, alleging that when Lin had served as prefect of Shuozhou and Zhongsi as military governor of Hedong, Zhongsi had said, "I was raised in the palace together with the Loyal Prince from an early age; I mean to honor and support the Crown Prince."

sentences.zh: 玄宗大怒，因征入朝，令三司推訊之，幾陷極刑。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was greatly enraged, summoned him to court, and had the Three Departments investigate; he nearly fell into capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong flew into a rage, summoned him to court, and ordered the Three Departments to investigate; he came within a hair's breadth of the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 會哥舒翰代忠嗣為隴右節度，特承恩顧，因奏忠嗣之枉，詞甚懇切，請以己官爵贖罪。

translations.literal: When Geshu Han replaced Zhongsi as Longyou military governor, especially favored by grace, he memorialized Zhongsi's injustice in very earnest words and asked to redeem the crime with his own rank.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han, who replaced Zhongsi as military governor of Longyou and enjoyed exceptional imperial favor, memorialized on Zhongsi's behalf in the most earnest terms, pleading to forfeit his own rank to redeem Zhongsi's guilt.

sentences.zh: 玄宗怒稍解。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong's anger eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's wrath eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 十一月，貶漢陽太守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was demoted to Hanyang prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was demoted to prefect of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 七載，量移漢東郡太守。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Handong prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 7 (748) he was transferred to prefect of Handong.

sentences.zh: 明年，暴卒，年四十五。

translations.literal: The next year he died suddenly, age forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died suddenly, at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 子震，天寶中秘書丞。

translations.literal: His son Zhen was a Secretariat aide under Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen served as an aide in the Secretariat during the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 其後哥舒翰大舉兵伐石堡城，拔之，死者大半，竟如忠嗣之言，當代稱為名將。

translations.literal: Later Geshu Han raised a great army to attack Shibao Fortress, took it, and more than half died—exactly as Zhongsi had said; his age called him a famed general.
translations.idiomatic: Later Geshu Han mounted a major campaign against Shibao Fortress and took it, but more than half his men died—just as Zhongsi had foretold. His contemporaries hailed him as a great general.

sentences.zh: 先是，忠嗣之在朔方也，每至互市時，即高估馬價以誘之，諸蕃聞之，競來求市，來輒買之。

translations.literal: Before this, when Zhongsi was in Shuofang, each time the border markets opened he inflated horse prices to lure them; the various tribes heard and raced to sell; all who came he bought.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Zhongsi was in Shuofang, whenever the frontier markets opened he bid up horse prices to draw sellers in. The tribes heard of it and flocked to trade; every horse offered, he bought.

sentences.zh: 故蕃馬益少，而漢軍益壯。

translations.literal: Thus barbarian horses grew fewer while Han troops grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the tribes' horses grew scarce while the Han armies grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 及至河、隴，又奏請徙朔方、河東戎馬九千匹以實之，其軍又壯。

translations.literal: When he reached He-Long he also memorialized to move nine thousand war horses from Shuofang and Hedong to fill them out, and that army grew strong again.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached He-Long he memorialized to transfer nine thousand war horses from Shuofang and Hedong to stock his command, and those forces grew strong again.

sentences.zh: 迄於天寶末，戰馬蕃息。

translations.literal: By the end of Tianbao, war horses multiplied abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: By the close of the Tianbao era, war horses had multiplied in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，追贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying he was posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying 1 (762) he was posthumously appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：郭虔瓘、郭知運、王君㚟、張守珪、牛仙客、王忠嗣，立功邊域，為世虎臣，班超、傅介子之流也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Guo Qianguan, Guo Zhiyun, Wang Jun, Zhang Shougui, Niu Xianke, and Wang Zhongsi won merit on the frontier and were tiger generals of their age, in the line of Ban Chao and Fu Jiezi.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Guo Qianguan, Guo Zhiyun, Wang Jun, Zhang Shougui, Niu Xianke, and Wang Zhongsi won distinction on the frontier and stood as the tiger generals of their age—men in the tradition of Ban Chao and Fu Jiezi.

sentences.zh: 然虔瓘以萬人征西，請給公乘、熟食，可謂謀之不臧矣。

translations.literal: Yet Qianguan, marching west with ten thousand men, asked for public carts and cooked food—one may say his planning was ill-advised.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Qianguan marched west with ten thousand men he demanded government carts and hot rations—hardly sound planning.

sentences.zh: 君㚟以父執登陴，兵竟不出，此則不知門外之事，義斷恩也。

translations.literal: Jun mounted the wall at his father's command yet the troops never left the gate—this shows ignorance of affairs beyond the gate; duty severed kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Jun climbed the wall at his father's order, yet his troops never marched out—proof that he did not grasp what lay beyond the gate; duty had cut through affection.

sentences.zh: 守珪以至誠感神，取材成堰，與夫耿恭拜井，有何異焉？

translations.literal: Shougui moved the gods by utmost sincerity and timbered a dam—how does this differ from Geng Gong's praying for a well?
translations.idiomatic: Shougui moved heaven by the depth of his sincerity and built a dam from timber—what difference is there from Geng Gong kneeling to pray for a well?

sentences.zh: 仙客爰自方隅，驟登廊廟，顯招物議，獨善其身，蓋才有不周，昧於陳力就列。

translations.literal: Xianke from a remote corner soared to the hall of state, plainly inviting public criticism and saving only himself—his talent was not rounded, blind to offering strength in due office.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke rose from a remote corner to the central court in a single leap, inviting open criticism while looking after himself alone—his gifts were incomplete, and he did not understand how to bring his strength to bear in office.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣因青蠅之點，幾危其身，讒人之言，誠可畏也！

translations.literal: Zhongsi, by the spots of green flies, nearly lost his life—the words of slanderers are truly dreadful!
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi, stained by the speck of a fly, nearly lost his life—the words of slanderers are truly to be feared!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：隴山之西，幽陵之北，爰有戎夷，世為殘賊。

translations.literal: Praise says: West of Long Mountains, north of You Ridge, there dwell barbarians who generation upon generation ravage as cruel bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: West of the Long Mountains, north of You Ridge, barbarians dwell who generation after generation raid and ravage.

sentences.zh: 二郭、二王，守珪、仙客，禦寇之功，存乎方策。

translations.literal: Two Guos, two Wangs, Shougui, Xianke—the merit of repelling invaders lives in the written records.
translations.idiomatic: The two Guos, the two Wangs, Shougui, Xianke—their deeds in defense against the enemy endure in the annals.
